brief:
Israel's president opened deliberations Wednesday on whom to task with forming a government following an election that left neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor rival Gadi Eisenkot with a parliamentary majority, Al-Monitor reported. The outcome highlighted deep divisions within the country after a contentious campaign.

The president's consultations mark the formal start of coalition negotiations that will determine which candidate receives the mandate to assemble a governing majority. Neither leading contender secured enough seats to govern independently, forcing backroom negotiations with smaller parties whose support will prove decisive in the coming weeks.
dek: Israel's president begins deliberations on Wednesday on whom to task to form a government, with neither veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor rival Gadi Eisenkot holding enough seats after a divisive election.
title: Israel's president begins government formation talks after inconclusive election
